pairs: Just as with the dividing of the waters,
ita cor regis in manu Domini:
so also is the heart of the king in the hand of the Lord.
He shall bend it whichever way he wills.
Omnis via viri recta sibi videtur:
Every way of a man seems right to himself.
Facere misericordiam et judicium magis placet Domino quam victimæ.
To do mercy and judgment is more pleasing to the Lord than sacrifices.
To lift up the eyes is to enlarge the heart.
The lamp of the impious is sin.
The intentions of the robust continually bring forth abundance.
omnis autem piger semper in egestate est.
But all the lazy are continually in need.
Qui congregat thesauros lingua mendacii vanus et excors est,
Whoever gathers treasures by a lying tongue is vain and heartless.
And he will stumble into the snares of death.
The robberies of the impious will drag them down,
because they were not willing to do judgment.
The perverse way of a man is foreign.
Melius est sedere in angulo domatis,
It is better to sit in a corner of the attic,
The soul of the impious desires evil;
he will not take pity on his neighbor.

The just thinks carefully about the house of the impious,
so that he may draw the impious away from evil.
Qui obturat aurem suam ad clamorem pauperis, et ipse clamabit,
Whoever blocks his ears to the outcry of the poor shall also cry out himself,
and he will not be heeded.
et donum in sinu indignationem maximam.
And a gift concealed in the bosom extinguishes the greatest indignation.
It is gladness for the just to do judgment;
and it is dread for those who work iniquity.
Vir qui erraverit a via doctrinæ in cœtu gigantum commorabitur.
A man who wanders astray from the way of doctrine will linger in the company of the giants.
Qui diligit epulas in egestate erit;
Whoever loves a feast will be in deprivation.
qui amat vinum et pinguia non ditabitur.
Whoever loves wine and fatness will not be enriched.
The impious is given over instead of the just,
and the iniquitous is given over in place of the upright.
Melius est habitare in terra deserta quam cum muliere rixosa
It is better to live in a deserted land,
than with a quarrelsome and emotional woman.
as well as oil, in the habitations of the just.

Qui sequitur justitiam et misericordiam inveniet vitam,
Whoever follows justice and mercy shall discover life,
The wise has ascended the city of the strong,
and he has torn down the bulwark of its confidence.
Qui custodit os suum et linguam suam custodit ab angustiis animam suam.
Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from anguish.

if he, in anger, acts according to pride.

because they are offered out of wickedness.

The impious man insolently hardens his face.
qui autem rectus est corrigit viam suam.
